issues.issue: Undefined capitalized terms are imported from the Pooling and Servicing Agreement, a document not attached, so terms actually used in the operative text such as "Material Defect" and "MOM Loan" in Section 6(a) have no meaning within this instrument. A court would have to decide whether the PSA definitions govern and what happens where none exists.

The definition uses the shorthand "Accredited" as a defined party although that term is nowhere defined in this Agreement. Its referent must be inferred from Exhibit C of the attached Underlying EMC Purchase Agreement.
"Accredited" is used as though defined but no definition of that entity appears in this Agreement. The class of Accredited Mortgage Loans therefore depends on an undefined identifier.

The dollar figures for the Acquisition Price are blank or garbled ("cash in an amount equal to $ i"; "an amount equal to of"), so the price term cannot be read off the instrument. A court asked to fix the consideration would have nothing in the text to work with.

"Covered" is defined only by reference to Appendix E of Standard & Poor's Glossary, an external and undated document whose content the parties do not reproduce. Which version of that glossary governs is left open.

Section 2(a) requires each Mortgage Loan Seller to sell loans with an aggregate Cut-off Date balance "equal to the Cut-off Date Balance," yet this definition fixes a single pool-wide figure. Read together the two provisions cannot both be satisfied by two sellers.
The definition breaks off mid-phrase with an unclosed quotation ("in such capacity, the “Custodian"), leaving the defined term incomplete on its face.

This definition and the Wells Fargo Custodial Agreement definition both define "Custodian," so the single term carries two different referents in the same definitional section. Provisions referring to "the related Custodian" must be construed to pick between them.

"Scheduled Payment" is used in the definition but is not defined in this Agreement; the operative provisions elsewhere speak of "Monthly Payment." The reader must import a term from the Pooling and Servicing Agreement to apply it.

An "EMC Mortgage Loan" is defined by who sold it, while "MSMCH Represented Mortgage Loans" is defined by who originated it, so a loan sold by EMC can also be a loan MSMCH represents upon. The overlap leaves it uncertain which seller's warranty regime governs such a loan.

The catch-all "or similar loan under any other applicable state, federal or local law" sits against the enumerated labels "high cost home," "threshold," "covered," "high risk home" and "predatory," so its reach is uncertain under ejusdem generis. Whether a given state statute produces a "similar" loan is a question the words do not answer.

The phrase "creating a first or second lien on or first or second priority ownership interest in an estate in fee simple in real property" is grammatically tangled and confines Mortgages to fee simple estates. Whether leasehold-secured or co-op loans qualify cannot be read off the words.

The definition is left indefinite on its face — "certain" loans "and certain other assets as described in the Prospectus Supplement" — so the population of Mortgage Loans is fixed only by an external offering document. What "certain other assets" are included cannot be determined from the Agreement.
Item (29) reads "a code indicating whether the Mortgage Loan is has a balloon payment," a plain drafting error in an enumerated data field.

This 33-item definition of the Mortgage Loan Schedule does not match the 25-item list in Exhibit 2, to which Section 3 directs the parties for the schedule's contents. The two lists differ in substance (e.g. street address and Mortgagor's name appear only in Exhibit 2), so what the schedule must contain is contested.

The definition says the rate is that "borne by a Mortgage Note as stated herein," but no rate is stated in this Agreement; the drafter plainly meant "therein," i.e., in the Mortgage Note. The error makes the definition circular as written.

The class is defined by originator (Aames, Aegis, Decision One, First NLC, MILA, New Century, Option One, Wilmington) and so excludes Fremont and Accredited loans, yet Section 10(b)(18) and the Accredited backstop paragraph purport to make representations within Section 10(b) about exactly those excluded loans. The scope of MSMCH's warranty obligation cannot be reconciled across those provisions.
"Piggyback Loan" is defined but the term appears nowhere in the operative provisions of this Agreement, leaving the definition without work to do.

Clause (iii) is garbled — "in connection with any violation of such Mortgage Loan of any anti-predatory lending laws" — so the costs and damages component of the repurchase price is hard to apply as written.

The definition conditions substitution on "the requirements stated herein," but this Agreement states no eligibility requirements for a Replacement Mortgage Loan anywhere; only the Underlying EMC Purchase Agreement's "Qualified Substitute Mortgage Loan" definition supplies criteria. Whether those criteria govern the substitution right in Section 10 is left open.

The definition describes the Underlying EMC Purchase Agreement as "between EMC and MSMCH," but the agreement actually attached as Exhibit 3 is between EMC and Morgan Stanley Mortgage Capital Inc., a different entity from Morgan Stanley Mortgage Capital Holdings LLC. Which document and which counterparty is meant is a genuine question.

"Value" is defined here as the lesser of appraisal and sales price, while the representations in Section 10 turn on "Appraised Value," defined in the attached Underlying EMC Purchase Agreement simply as the appraisal figure. The two valuation standards sit side by side without a rule of priority.

This definition designates Wells Fargo as "the Custodian" while the Deutsche Bank Custodial Agreement definition gives the same defined term to Deutsche Bank. References elsewhere to "the related Custodian" must be construed to resolve the duplication.

The obligation is keyed to loans "having an aggregate outstanding principal balance as of the Cut-off Date equal to the Cut-off Date Balance" for each Mortgage Loan Seller, although the Cut-off Date Balance is one pool-wide number; it also sells an interest in "the Swap Agreements," a term never defined. Both leave the sale obligation indeterminate.

The condition precedent is "the conditions set forth in Section 11 hereof," but Section 11 assigns the Accredited and Fremont letters and contains no conditions; the closing conditions are in Section 14. The cross-reference must be construed or corrected.

Payment of the Acquisition Price is made conditional on "the conditions set forth in Section 11 hereof," but Section 11 contains no conditions; the closing conditions appear in Section 14. A court would have to decide whether the payment obligation is conditioned at all.

Section 3 directs that the Mortgage Loan Schedule set forth "the information listed on Exhibit 2," while the Section 1 definition of Mortgage Loan Schedule prescribes a different 33-item list. The required content of the schedule cannot be determined without choosing between them.
